insight: The wind potential map shows how strong and steady the wind is across the Philippines, scored from 0 (weak) to 100 (very strong). The average score for the 84 provinces with data is about 43, which means most places have modest wind. The highest score, 63.6, appears in Batanes, where wind speeds at 100 m height reach about 6.36 m/s – enough to be called "high" potential. Provinces like Cavite (57.8) and Albay (53.1) fall in the "moderate" range because their wind speeds are around 3.2 m/s at ground level and 5.6 m/s higher up. These numbers are good enough for small turbines but not for large farms. On the lower end, Cotabato (27.1), Sarangani (28.0) and Quirino (29.6) score below 30, reflecting wind speeds near 2.7‑3.0 m/s at 100 m – too light for most commercial projects. Even provinces near the sea or volcanoes can stay in the moderate group if the wind isn’t consistently strong; exposure to open water or steep terrain helps, but only when the wind keeps blowing at useful speeds. Overall, most of the country sits in the moderate to low band, with just one province reaching high potential.
